newsitem.title: USA: Speedway Motorsports sweetens N.C. Motor bid.
newsitem.headline: Speedway Motorsports sweetens N.C. Motor bid.

text.p: Speedway Motorsports Inc. said Wednesday it raised its takeover offer for North Carolina Motor Speedway Inc. to $32 a share or $71.6 million in cash or stock.
Speedway said the offer is at least 72 percent more than the latest offer by Penske Motorsports Inc., a promoter and marketer of professional motor sports.
Penske on April 1 offered either $14 in cash per share, or stock based on a complicated formula.
Speedway, a speedway owner and operator based in Concord, N.C., said its offer is 39 percent more than its own cash bid of $23 a share made two weeks ago.
Under the revised offer, North Carolina Motor stockholders may choose to receive $32 in cash, or the equivalent amount in Speedway common shares for each share of North Carolina Motor.
North Carolina Motor is a one-mile oval track in Rockingham, N.C., about 80 miles east of Charlotte, N.C. The speedway was built in 1965 by a group of local investors.
Its two National Stock Car Racing Winston Cup Series events are the "Goodwrench Service 400" in February and the "ACDelco 400" in October.
Speedway stock fell 32.5 cents to $22.75, while Penske's fell 50 cents to $30.75 on Nasdaq.
